intro: Families around the world eat different foods. They wear different clothes. They say hello in different words. They keep different holidays. In this unit, you will visit many of them.
You will meet rice, tortillas, bread and injera. You will see a kimono, a sari and a huipil. You will learn hola, bonjour, ni hao and namaste.
By the end, you can name customs from many places. You can ask a friend kind questions about home. You can say hello and thank you in new words.
bigQuestion: How do food, clothes, words and holidays make each family special?

timeline.t: We share bread from home and learn its name.
We try eating with chopsticks, a fork and the hand.
We look at clothes for hot and cold places.
We see special clothes for special days.
We learn to try new food kindly.
We say hello in four languages and learn a bow.
We learn about holidays families keep.
We make a class chart of thank-you words.

words.d: a main food that people eat very often
a flat, round bread made from corn or wheat
a soft, flat bread from Ethiopia with tiny holes
a way a group of people has done something for a long time
a word or action used to say hello
the words and ways people use to talk and write
the food, words, clothes, beliefs and holidays a group shares
treating people and the things they care about with kindness

choices: a main food people eat very often
a food for one party only
test.why: A staple food, like rice or tortillas, is eaten again and again.

test.q: Which bread is made from teff?
test.why: Injera from Ethiopia is made from a tiny grain called teff.
Chopsticks pinch food. A fork pokes food.

test.q: What do people in cold places wear?
test.why: Thick coats, hats and boots keep people warm in the cold.

choices: Maya women in Guatemala and Mexico
test.why: The huipil is a woven top worn by many Maya women.

test.q: Which word is a hello in Mandarin Chinese?
test.why: Ni hao is hello in Mandarin Chinese.

test.q: About how many languages do people speak?
test.why: People in the world speak about 7,000 languages.

test.q: What do families do on Día de los Muertos?
test.why: Día de los Muertos is a day to remember loved ones.

test.q: A friend brings a new food. What is kind?
choices: Ask its name and try a small bite.
test.why: Being respectful means asking, trying a small bite and using kind words.

write.prompt: Why is it good to learn about other families' food, clothes, words and holidays? Tell your answer. Use two things you learned in this unit.
tips: Start with your answer in one sentence.
Name two things from the unit, like injera or Diwali.
Use a unit word, like custom or culture.
You can draw a picture and write one line under it.
